system:
You write four sections of an analysis report for a biomedical data-analysis agent: Conclusion, Evidence, Limits, Recommendations.
You receive the scientific question, the compiled objective, what was done, and a table of named facts.

Hard rules
- Every number you mention must be written as a placeholder {{fact_key}} using a key from the table. Never type a digit yourself (plan ids such as P3 and the terms PAM50, H&E are allowed).
- Say only what the facts support. The conclusion must be no stronger than the evaluator's unified result allows, must answer the question that was asked, and must stay inside the stated scope.
- Report unfavourable facts plainly (a selected plan that is not the best, a self-reported score above the unified one, an inconclusive interval, few genes). Do not soften or pad.
- Plain, direct English. No bullet inside the Conclusion. No headings inside your text.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"conclusion": [two or three paragraphs], "evidence": [three to five paragraphs], "limits": [four to seven sentences, one per item], "recommendations": [three to five sentences, one per item]}
prompt:
SCIENTIFIC QUESTION:
Using the paired RNA and ATAC measurements, learn the cross-modal relationship. For cells of the same donor that took no part in training and for which only ATAC is provided, for which genes can the variation in RNA expression be predicted reliably?

OBJECTIVE:
{
 "estimand": "Per-gene Pearson correlation between ATAC-predicted and binomial-thinned log-normalised RNA across unseen donor cells, and per-gene correlation gain over the ATAC cluster-mean baseline.",
 "forbidden_inputs": [
  "Held-out cells' RNA counts (full or thinned halves) during training, tuning, or prediction",
  "Held-out cells' ATAC counts during model training, preprocessing, latent-space fitting, clustering, or hyperparameter selection",
  "Curated WNN cell-type annotations as model inputs for unseen cells or as evaluation ground truth",
  "Smoothed, imputed, denoised, or unthinned full-depth RNA expression as the validation scoring target",
  "Validation-split cells' RNA or ATAC during training, feature transformation, baseline clustering, or model selection",
  "External donor datasets, atlases, or pretrained model weights outside the provided paired Multiome measurements"
 ],
 "conclusion_options": [
  "Unjudgeable due to measurement noise: for every in-scope gene, the RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling fails to exceed the cell-permutation null.",
  "Confounded by sequencing depth: judgeable genes exist, but ATAC predictors fail to exceed the technical ATAC-depth baseline across unseen donor cells.",
  "No gene predicted beyond cell identity: predictors beat the depth baseline, but no judgeable in-scope gene significantly beats the ATAC cluster-mean baseline at 5% FDR.",
  "Specific genes predicted beyond cell identity: predictors beat technical floors, and an identified non-empty set of judgeable genes beats the ATAC cluster-mean baseline at 5% FDR."
 ],
 "conclusion_scope": "Applies solely to unseen granulocyte-depleted PBMCs from this single healthy donor under the same Multiome assay; shows nothing about generalisation across other donors, tissues, disease states, granulocytes, or causal gene regulation."
}

  },
  {

   "name": "Cluster-Reweighted Negative Binomial Chromatin-to-Count Translation Network",
   "complexity": "ambitious",
   "component": "translation_network"
  },
  {
   "id": "P4",

   "complexity": "ambitious",
   "component": "residual_over_cluster_mean"
  },
  {
   "id": "P5",
   "name": "Cluster-Balanced Hyperspherical Contrastive Alignment with Multi-Scale MLP Readout",
   "complexity": "ambitious",
   "component": "contrastive_pretrain_head"
  },
  {
   "id": "P6",
   "name": "Gene-Adaptive Multi-Mechanism Chromatin Stacking Ensemble",
   "complexity": "ambitious",
   "component": "stacking_ensemble"
  }
 ],
 "tournament_ranking": [
  "P1",
  "P6",
  "P5",
  "P3",
  "P4",
  "P2"
 ],
 "selected": "P1",
 "selected_summary": "Each cell's ATAC profile is projected into a depth-filtered Latent Semantic Indexing space fitted strictly on training cells, and ridge regression predicts expression across all 11,282 target genes. Using nested five-fold cross-validation over three seeds, predictions on unseen cells are scored against binomial-thinned RNA alongside technical floors, the ATAC cluster-mean baseline, and an RNA noise ceiling. Paired bootstraps with false-discovery control identify which judgeable genes exceed cell identity. This simple reference quantifies what global linear chromatin state achieves alone.",
 "audit_trail": [
  {
   "plan_id": "P1",
   "rank": 1,
   "passed": true,
   "blocking_failures": [],
   "reviewer_decision": "accept"
  }
 ],
 "wording_limits": [
  "Must not claim the result generalises to other donors, tissues, disease states or granulocytes.",
  "Must not claim the predictions reveal causal gene regulation or chromatin-to-expression mechanisms.",
  "Must not describe RNA as predicted 'accurately' or 'reliably' in absolute terms; mean r is about 0.145.",
  "Must not claim P1 outperforms ridge, PLS or other simple learners.",
  "Must not present the 4536 claimed genes as confirmed on the held-out hidden cells; they are a development-set estimate.",
  "Must not make claims about the 309 unjudgeable genes, in either direction.",
  "Must not describe the gain over cell identity as large; it is a mean of about 0.012 r."
 ],
 "difficulties": [
  "D1 measurement_noise: RNA counts are 85.3% zeros (median 3800 UMIs per cell). Splitting each cell's reads into two independent halves, a gene's value in one half correlates with the other half at a median r of 0.111 across 11282 in-scope genes (90th percentile 0.306).",
  "D2 class_imbalance: The provided annotation has 19 cell types in the development set, from 1936 cells (CD14 Mono) down to 15 (Plasma).",
  "D3 multiple_comparisons: 11282 genes are in scope and each gets its own test.",
  "D4 label_provenance: The cell-type annotation supplied with the development cells was produced by clustering both modalities jointly (weighted nearest neighbours) and curating the clusters by hand. It is not an independent measurement.",
  "D5 technical_confounding: ATAC depth and RNA depth are correlated across cells (r = 0.36 on the log scale). A model that sees only ATAC depth reaches a mean per-gene r of 0.032.",
  "D6 strong_baseline: Predicting each cell by the mean expression of its ATAC cluster (k = 20, chosen by cross-validation inside the development set) gives a mean per-gene r of 0.130; ridge regression on the ATAC latent space gives 0.143; the RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling is 0.194.",
  "D7 statistical_power: With thousands of cells a correlation as small as 0.037 already exceeds 95% of the permutation null (3124 held-out cells will be scored)."
 ]
}

n_candidates = 6 : number of candidate plans in the frozen pool
n_ambitious = 5 : candidates classed as ambitious
selected_plan = P1 : id of the plan the agent selected and reported
selected_name = Nested LSI Multi-Output Ridge Reference : name of the selected plan
tournament_champion = P1 : plan ranked first by the tournament
order_consistency = 100% : share of plan pairs judged the same way in both presentation orders
n_matches = 30 : number of judged matches
selected_true_rank = 2 : rank of the selected plan among all candidates under the evaluator's unified score (1 = best)
best_true_plan = P6 : plan with the best unified score
selection_gap = 0.0031 : unified score of the best candidate minus that of the selected plan
audit_outcome = answer_reported : outcome of the audit
n_genes_in_scope = 11282 : genes in scope
n_genes_judgeable = 10741 : in-scope genes whose ceiling is above the permutation null on held-out cells
ceiling_r = 0.193 : mean per-gene r of the RNA-to-RNA ceiling
cluster_mean_r = 0.134 : mean per-gene r of the cell-type (cluster-mean) baseline
ridge_r = 0.147 : mean per-gene r of ridge regression on the ATAC latent space
gene_activity_r = 0.036 : mean per-gene r of the gene-activity score
depth_r = 0.032 : mean per-gene r from ATAC depth alone
selected_true_r = 0.147 : unified score of the selected plan: mean per-gene r on held-out cells
selected_self_r = 0.145 : score the selected plan reported for itself in its full run
selected_inflation = -0.002 : self-reported minus unified score of the selected plan
mean_inflation = -0.003 : mean of self-reported minus unified score over candidates
selected_fraction_of_ceiling = 76% : unified score of the selected plan as a share of the ceiling
selected_delta_vs_cluster = +0.0133 : mean per-gene r of the selected plan minus the cluster-mean baseline on held-out cells
n_beyond = 2570 : genes the selected plan predicts beyond cell type on held-out cells (FDR 5%)
n_not_beyond = 8171 : judgeable genes not beyond the cell-type baseline
n_cannot_judge = 541 : genes that cannot be judged
share_beyond = 23.9% : genes predicted beyond cell type as a share of judgeable genes
n_claimed = 4536 : genes the plan itself claimed from development cells
replication_rate = 39% : share of the plan's claimed genes confirmed on held-out cells
within_cluster_r = 0.057 : mean per-gene r of the selected plan inside clusters
max_beyond_any_plan = 4080 : largest number of genes beyond cell type achieved by any candidate

conclusion: In unseen granulocyte-depleted peripheral blood mononuclear cells from this individual healthy donor assayed under the paired Multiome protocol, single-cell RNA expression variation is not predicted accurately or reliably in absolute terms from ATAC accessibility alone, as the selected predictor {{selected_plan}} ({{selected_name}}) reaches a modest mean per-gene Pearson correlation of {{selected_true_r}} against binomial-thinned RNA counts. When cross-modal predictability is evaluated relative to technical floors and coarse chromatin cell identity across {{n_genes_in_scope}} in-scope genes, {{n_genes_judgeable}} genes have an RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling above the permutation null on held-out cells, whereas {{n_cannot_judge}} unjudgeable genes fail to clear measurement noise and support no claim in either direction. Among the {{n_genes_judgeable}} judgeable genes, {{selected_plan}} exceeds both the ATAC sequencing-depth baseline ({{depth_r}}) and local gene-activity scores ({{gene_activity_r}}), and predicts a specific subset of {{n_beyond}} genes ({{share_beyond}}) significantly better than the ATAC cluster-mean baseline after false-discovery-rate control, while {{n_not_beyond}} judgeable genes show no statistically significant improvement beyond cluster identity.

Even with statistically significant gains on {{n_beyond}} genes, most predictable cross-modal variation reflects coarse cell-type composition rather than fine within-type state. On held-out cells, the ATAC cluster-mean baseline alone attains a mean per-gene correlation of {{cluster_mean_r}} out of the {{ceiling_r}} RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling, so {{selected_plan}} ({{selected_fraction_of_ceiling}} of the ceiling) adds a small mean correlation gain of {{selected_delta_vs_cluster}} and reaches a mean within-cluster correlation of only {{within_cluster_r}}. Gene-level discovery from development cells also generalised poorly: {{selected_plan}} claimed {{n_claimed}} genes beyond cell identity during development, but only {{replication_rate}} of those claimed genes replicated on the held-out split. Moreover, although the tournament chose {{tournament_champion}} out of {{n_candidates}} candidates, {{selected_plan}} placed at rank {{selected_true_rank}} under unified held-out scoring, trailing {{best_true_plan}} by {{selection_gap}} in mean correlation while the largest set of genes predicted beyond cell identity by any candidate reached {{max_beyond_any_plan}}.

These conclusions apply strictly to unseen granulocyte-depleted peripheral blood mononuclear cells from this healthy donor measured with the same paired Multiome assay. They describe statistical association between global chromatin accessibility and thinned transcript counts within this sample, and establish nothing regarding generalisation to other donors, tissues, disease states, or granulocytes, nor do they demonstrate causal chromatin-to-expression gene regulation.
evidence: To prevent target leakage and smoothing artefacts, predictions for unseen donor cells were evaluated strictly against binomial-thinned log-normalised RNA counts while fitting all feature transformations and clusterings exclusively on training splits. Across {{n_genes_in_scope}} in-scope genes on the held-out split, severe single-cell transcript sparsity restricts the mean split-half RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling to {{ceiling_r}}. Exactly {{n_genes_judgeable}} genes exhibit a held-out noise ceiling above the cell-permutation null and are therefore judgeable, whereas {{n_cannot_judge}} genes fall within measurement noise and cannot be evaluated in either direction. Technical covariation with ATAC sequencing depth alone yields a mean per-gene correlation of {{depth_r}}, and local chromatin gene-activity aggregation reaches only {{gene_activity_r}}, whereas assigning each unseen cell the mean expression of its ATAC-derived cluster achieves {{cluster_mean_r}}, confirming that discrete lineage identity accounts for most cross-modal signal.

The selected reference model {{selected_plan}} ({{selected_name}}) projects unseen ATAC profiles into a training-fitted, depth-filtered Latent Semantic Indexing space and predicts log-normalised expression across all {{n_genes_in_scope}} genes via multi-output ridge regression. Under unified held-out evaluation, {{selected_plan}} achieves a mean per-gene Pearson correlation of {{selected_true_r}}, matching the ATAC latent-space ridge benchmark ({{ridge_r}}) and capturing {{selected_fraction_of_ceiling}} of the {{ceiling_r}} noise ceiling without outperforming standard linear learners. Compared against the {{cluster_mean_r}} ATAC cluster-mean baseline, continuous latent chromatin state yields a small mean per-gene correlation gain of {{selected_delta_vs_cluster}}, and mean per-gene correlation computed within ATAC clusters is {{within_cluster_r}}.

Paired testing across the {{n_genes_judgeable}} judgeable genes on held-out cells shows that {{n_beyond}} genes ({{share_beyond}}) achieve a statistically significant correlation gain over the ATAC cluster-mean baseline after false-discovery-rate control, whereas {{n_not_beyond}} judgeable genes do not beat cluster identity. Comparing development estimates with held-out performance reveals a sharp divergence between global score stability and per-gene discovery stability: {{selected_plan}} self-reported a development mean correlation of {{selected_self_r}}, which was slightly conservative relative to its unified held-out score of {{selected_true_r}} (inflation of {{selected_inflation}}), yet its development run claimed {{n_claimed}} genes beyond cell identity, of which only {{replication_rate}} replicated on the held-out cells.

The frozen candidate pool comprised {{n_candidates}} plans, pairing the simple reference {{selected_plan}} against {{n_ambitious}} ambitious architectures covering sparse cis-regulatory neural networks, cluster-reweighted negative-binomial translation, residual gradient boosting over cluster means, contrastive alignment, and multi-mechanism stacking. Across {{n_matches}} judged pairwise tournament matches, {{tournament_champion}} ranked at the top with {{order_consistency}} presentation-order consistency and passed audit review, and candidate self-reported scores showed no upward bias on average relative to unified held-out scores (mean inflation {{mean_inflation}}). On the held-out cells, however, {{selected_plan}} placed at rank {{selected_true_rank}} behind {{best_true_plan}}, which outperformed {{selected_plan}} by a selection gap of {{selection_gap}} in mean per-gene correlation, while the highest number of held-out genes predicted beyond cell identity across all candidates reached {{max_beyond_any_plan}} compared with {{n_beyond}} for {{selected_plan}}.
limits: All observations come from granulocyte-depleted peripheral blood mononuclear cells of a single healthy donor under the same Multiome assay, providing no evidence of generalisation to other donors, tissues, disease states, or granulocytes.

Severe single-cell RNA measurement sparsity caps the mean split-half noise ceiling at {{ceiling_r}} across {{n_genes_in_scope}} in-scope genes and leaves {{n_cannot_judge}} genes completely unjudgeable on held-out cells.

Absolute predictive accuracy at the single-cell level remains low even among the {{n_genes_judgeable}} judgeable genes, with a mean held-out correlation of {{selected_true_r}}, a small mean gain of {{selected_delta_vs_cluster}} over the {{cluster_mean_r}} ATAC cluster-mean baseline, and a mean within-cluster correlation of {{within_cluster_r}}.

Per-gene discovery beyond cell identity showed substantial split-to-split instability, as only {{replication_rate}} of the {{n_claimed}} development-claimed genes replicated on held-out evaluation ({{n_beyond}} confirmed genes overall).

Tournament model selection chose {{selected_plan}} (held-out rank {{selected_true_rank}}) over the top held-out candidate {{best_true_plan}}, forfeiting {{selection_gap}} in mean per-gene correlation and capturing {{n_beyond}} genes beyond cell identity compared with up to {{max_beyond_any_plan}} in the candidate pool.

Predictions from global Latent Semantic Indexing components reflect correlational chromatin-to-RNA covariation dominated by abundant immune lineages rather than cis-regulatory mechanisms or causal transcriptional control.
recommendations: Restrict any downstream use of ATAC-predicted expression within this donor context to the {{n_beyond}} held-out-confirmed genes or apply cross-split stability selection, given that development-only discovery ({{n_claimed}} claimed genes) achieved only a {{replication_rate}} held-out replication rate.

Prioritise gene-adaptive multi-mechanism stacking architectures such as {{best_true_plan}} over global ridge regression alone ({{selected_plan}}) when seeking to maximise gene recovery beyond cell identity, as candidate models closed a {{selection_gap}} correlation gap and expanded confirmed genes up to {{max_beyond_any_plan}}.

Align model-selection criteria directly with paired out-of-fold correlation gains over the {{cluster_mean_r}} ATAC cluster-mean baseline and within-cluster correlation ({{within_cluster_r}}) so that tournament ranking does not over-penalise expressive architectures that improve fine-grained prediction.

Acquire paired Multiome datasets spanning multiple donors and enriched for rare immune populations before testing whether chromatin-based expression predictors generalise beyond donor-specific blood cell composition.
